name: Prize crossword No 22,387
preamble: Solve the clues and fit the solutions into the diagram jigsaw-wise wherever they will go.

clue.text: Painter backing teacher in assembly

indicators.note: backing suggests moving backwards, so the word for teacher is read from its end
in tells us one piece sits inside the other, enclosed by the word for assembly

blocks.note: a moot is an old word for a meeting or assembly of people
pupils address a male teacher as Sir

explanation.surface: An artist is supporting a schoolteacher at a school assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: Berthe MORISOT was a French Impressionist; the reversed teacher goes between the two Os of the assembly word.
explanation.definitionFit: Berthe Morisot was a nineteenth-century French Impressionist artist, so she is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Single ship shows what's the soul of wit

blocks.note: single means one
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A lone vessel turns out to embody wit itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Polonius says brevity is the soul of wit, and a joke told in a single line is brevity itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a short quip; brevity being the soul of wit, as Hamlet puts it, the quip embodies it.

clue.text: Painter's not thus pictured Rex Day's fling

definitions.note: past participle: what a painter's subjects are not, the way the clue is phrased

indicators.note: a fling is a wild throw, so the letters are tossed about and land in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of the two names, the apostrophe and S belonging to the surface

explanation.surface: A man called Rex Day has a romantic fling that no artist would ever paint.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of Day's is not fodder; Day's fling reads as the fling of the name Rex Day.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter shows the outside of a sitter, never an image made by radiation through the body, which is how a radiographer pictures it.

clue.text: Step-dame's book about an arc that's trembly

definitions.note: possessive used as an adjective: belonging to a stepmother

indicators.note: something trembly shakes, so these letters are shaken into another order
about means around, so the book word wraps itself around the other letters

blocks.note: a novel is a book
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked stepmother's storybook is about a shaky arc.
explanation.walkthrough: NOVERCAL comes from the Latin noverca, stepmother; the shaken ARC sits before the final L of the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Novercal is a rare adjective meaning of or like a stepmother, from the Latin word for one.

clue.text: Painters' bit of stuff is heard at first

definitions.note: a possessive standing for a place belonging to painters, the Florence gallery

indicators.note: only a bit of the word is wanted, so its opening letters are dropped
heard tells us to take the sound of the word rather than its spelling
at first points to the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the end of the word, without its first two letters
the little word is pronounced with a Z sound, so it can be spelt that way
the first letter of the same small word

explanation.surface: Some painters' material is heard of before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The UFFIZI is the great art gallery in Florence; Araucaria uses the little word twice, once for its sound and once for its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uffizi in Florence houses the works of many Renaissance artists, so it is a gallery that belongs to painters.

clue.text: Painter king with Eleanor for Queen

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Nell is a pet form of Eleanor
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A court painter works for the king alongside Eleanor, for the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Godfrey KNELLER was principal court painter to English monarchs, which makes the royal surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Godfrey Kneller was a German-born portrait artist at the English court, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Painter, back, ran into 007

indicators.note: back tells us to read the following verb from right to left
into means going inside, so the verb is placed within the spy's name

blocks.note: 007 is the code number of the spy James Bond
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist dashes back and collides with James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre BONNARD was a French Post-Impressionist; the reversed verb goes before the final D of the spy's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Bonnard was a French artist known for intimate domestic scenes, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Painter, last away with what you will!

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
away and off both mean gone from a place
any means whichever you choose

explanation.surface: An artist is told to let the final item go and do whatever he likes.
explanation.walkthrough: Johann ZOFFANY was a German-born painter who worked in England; read Z off any.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Zoffany was a neoclassical portrait artist active in Georgian England, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Call back blood, foul harpy! Sacred list

indicators.note: back tells us the word for blood is written from right to left
foul means corrupted, so the letters of the monster are spoiled into a new order

blocks.note: hi is a greeting you might call out
gore is spilt blood
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone yells at a bloodthirsty harpy and then turns to a holy register.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation splits the clue in two; everything before it is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hierography is a description or catalogue of sacred things, from the Greek hieros, holy, and graphein, to write.

clue.text: Painter, South NZ, on Yorkshire head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken from the county name

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for south
New Zealand is made of islands, so it stands for an isle
the first letter of the county

explanation.surface: An artist travels from the south of New Zealand to the headlands of Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred SISLEY was an Anglo-French Impressionist landscape painter. Yorkshire is a large county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Sisley was an Impressionist known for landscapes around Paris, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Kind of hockey pitch that's full of floes

blocks.note: first meaning: the playing area for ice hockey, read as two words
second meaning: a wide expanse of floating sea ice

explanation.walkthrough: Hockey pitch suggests grass and sticks, but the first reading asks which kind of hockey is played on a frozen surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An icefield is a large sheet of ice at sea made up of floating floes, and ice hockey needs a frozen playing area.

clue.text: Painter king for Yanks to bathroom goes

blocks.note: first meaning: Augustus ..., the Welsh portrait painter
second meaning: American slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: An artist king who, being American, heads off to the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The word king is a third hint rather than a link: King John ruled England. Yanks are Americans, whose slang supplies the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus John was a celebrated Welsh artist, and in American slang a john is a lavatory or toilet.

clue.text: Orders painters' saint must follow straight

blocks.note: direct means straight, without a detour
St Ives in Cornwall is famous as an artists' colony

explanation.surface: A patron saint of artists must obey commands without deviation.
explanation.walkthrough: The saint is a place, not a person: St Ives in Cornwall drew many painters, so it is the painters' saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Directives are official instructions or commands issued by an authority, the same sense as plural orders.

clue.text: Painter on cigar leaf is displayed

indicators.note: something displayed is laid out for show, so these letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: the letters of the three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist's work is exhibited on a tobacco leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: On looks like a positional link, but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fra Angelico was an early Renaissance Florentine friar famous for frescoes, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Tune and verses bringing us to heaven

definitions.note: a participle phrase describing what the answer does, while the answer is a plural noun

blocks.note: an air is a tune
lines are verses of poetry

explanation.surface: Music and poetry lift the listener up to paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: Heaven in the surface means paradise, but in the definition it means the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Airline companies fly passengers up into the skies, which the heavens can mean in a literal sense.

clue.text: Length of bell? Pub session terminate

blocks.note: first meaning: the duration of a phone call, a bell being slang for a call
second meaning: what a landlord does at closing, ending the drinking

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to give someone a bell is to phone them. Pubs once rang a bell when the landlord announced that drinking was over.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who calls time announces closing, and read as two words the phrase also means the duration of a phone conversation.

clue.text: Camp? J's cardinal point when point is missed

indicators.note: missing a point means the small spur that turns one letter shape into another is taken away

blocks.note: Cardinal Richard Cushing of Boston was a close friend of Jack and Jackie Kennedy
the spur on the letter shape, the only difference between the first letter of the answer and that of the cardinal

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a camp is J's main compass direction once the point is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: A G whose spur is missed looks like a C, so GUSHING with its point missed would read as CUSHING, the cardinal.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp behaviour is exaggerated and theatrical, and gushing speech is likewise over-effusive and showily emotional.

clue.text: Painter heard to fail, one to F kin?

indicators.note: heard tells us to use the sound of the next word, spelt differently

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword painter
the F sound spelt as PH, the way it is in Greek-derived names

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a painter heard to fail is related to F.
explanation.walkthrough: F is the jigsaw's other answer beginning with F, FRA ANGELICO: the archangel RAPHAEL is kin to an angelic friar, and both are Renaissance painters.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael, like Fra Angelico, was an Italian Renaissance master, and his name is an archangel's, matching the angelic friar.

clue.text: Four at wharf: sea bird, first right, comes in

indicators.note: comes in means enters, so the bird and the following letters go inside the landing place

blocks.note: a quay is a wharf
a tern is a sea bird
A is first, as in A1
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Four people at a wharf watch as a sea bird, first on the right, comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaternary means consisting of four or in fours, from the Latin quaterni, four at a time.

clue.text: Painter in GP's report, a red

blocks.note: first meaning: the Venetian Renaissance master
second meaning: an auburn shade named after his favourite hair colour

explanation.surface: A doctor's report mentions an artist who is a communist.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle words are a hint by sound: a GP is a general practitioner, and the answer can be heard in that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian master, and titian is a bright reddish-brown colour seen in his portraits' hair.

clue.text: Cry of joy: drunk pipe - that's solvers' fill

indicators.note: a drunk staggers, so the letters of the next word lurch out of order
fill means go inside, so the jumbled letters sit within the solvers' pronoun

blocks.note: ye is an old word for you, the people addressed, here the solvers
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone whoops with delight after a smoke while doing the crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Yippee is an exclamation people shout when delighted, the same as an exultant shout or whoop.

clue.text: King and painter, king of nonsense scene

blocks.note: first meaning: Shakespeare's tragic monarch
second meaning: Edward ..., landscape painter and master of nonsense verse

explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear wrote limericks and The Owl and the Pussy-cat but also earned his living painting landscapes and birds.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic ruler, and Edward Lear was both an artist and the leading nonsense poet.

clue.text: Which device to use? Considering

blocks.note: first meaning: asking which tool one should do something with
second meaning: an idiom introducing the reasons for something

explanation.walkthrough: The question reads literally as asking what to do something with; the idiom means because of.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces causes, as in being busy because of work and family, which is the sense of the preposition considering.

clue.text: Varied page: new yacht appears on it

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the boat's letters are made over in a different order

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for page
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mixed page of a magazine features a picture of a new yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: Something patchy is uneven or inconsistent in quality, good in parts and poor in others, which is what varied can mean.

clue.text: Very cross, exploded a grenade

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so these letters fly apart and land rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of the weapon, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone furious set off a hand grenade.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the answer causes the explosion, but exploded is the instruction and the bomb is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enraged means being furious or extremely angry, which is what very cross describes.

clue.text: Painter's ever right with me dispersed

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered about, so the gathered letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist is always correct, and the crowd around the speaker breaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for is and joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was the Dutch Golden Age master of Girl with a Pearl Earring, so he is an example of a painter.
